summary: A governed lakehouse on object storage using Iceberg (default) with Trino for interactive SQL and Spark/Flink for ingestion and maintenance, coordinated by a single control-plane service backed by Postgres. The design is largely production-feasible, with clear operational targets, maintenance strategy, and failure-mode thinking, while keeping dependencies intentionally minimal.
strengths: Good core correctness model (object storage + transactional catalog) with practical ops details (file sizing, maintenance jobs, rewrite budgets, conflict handling)
Clear separation of compute workloads and a coherent governance/story for policy enforcement and auditing centered on Trino + a unified control plane
weaknesses: Control Service + Postgres is a critical bespoke control plane that can become a scaling/availability bottleneck; needs clearer multi-region/DR strategy and hardening for 2k users/20k tables (caching, read replicas, rate limits, SLO isolation)

Some hard parts are under-specified at scale: enforcing governance consistently outside Trino (SparkSQL path), GDPR deletes in immutable lakehouse semantics (delete files/compaction SLAs/verification), and operational security boundaries (IAM, key mgmt, tenant isolation)
